title: The Night Gallery
tagline: Bath, a winter night. The alarm has sealed every door.
intro: The Ashcombe Museum. A false alarm dropped the security shutters and locked the building, and nobody can get in or out. At 11:10 pm Beatrice Ashcombe, the director of the museum, is found dead in the sculpture hall. One of the four people left here did it.
public_facts: A false alarm dropped the security shutters and locked the building at about 8:30 pm. Nobody could come or go after that.
The patrons' reception ended at about 10:00 pm.
Beatrice Ashcombe, 66, the director of the museum, went to the sculpture hall at about 10:15 pm.
Beatrice Ashcombe was found dead in the sculpture hall at 11:10 pm by Cecily Ashcombe. She had been struck on the head.
The people here that night were: Cecily Ashcombe (Beatrice's sister), Laurence Vane (museum registrar), Joe Lambert (art handler), Rupert Sloane (a visitor).

solution.motive: Laurence Vane had been swapping small pieces from the stores for copies and selling the originals. Beatrice compared a coin in the stores with its old photograph and was going to call the police in the morning.
solution.method: At about 10:35 pm Laurence Vane went to the sculpture hall and argued with Beatrice, then struck her with a small bronze bust. He took the folder of dealers' receipts to the conservation studio and dissolved it in the solvent bath.

motives.text: To stop Beatrice exposing something they had done
To get control of The Ashcombe Museum
Revenge for something Beatrice did that day

evidence.name: Registry accession list
evidence.description: Laurence Vane's accession list from the registry. The last entry is timed 10:10 pm. The job is not finished.

evidence.name: Visitor pass stub
evidence.description: A late visitor pass issued to a pawnbroker for the members' room. It puts Cecily Ashcombe in the members' room from 10:30 pm to 10:52 pm.

evidence.name: Half-dissolved receipts
evidence.description: What is left of the folder of dealers' receipts, found in the conservation studio. Parts of it can still be read.

evidence.name: Laurence's blazer
evidence.description: Laurence Vane's blazer, left in the staff cloakroom. There is cleaning solvent on it.

evidence.name: Written reprimand
evidence.description: A formal reprimand to the art handler for a scratched frame. It is dated today and names Joe Lambert.

evidence.name: Collector's shopping list
evidence.description: A typed list from a private collector naming museum pieces and prices. It names Rupert Sloane.

cecily_ashcombe.name: Cecily Ashcombe
cecily_ashcombe.role: Beatrice Ashcombe's sister. She chairs the museum's friends and raises its money.
story_they_tell: After the patrons' reception I was resting in the flat upstairs.
Later I went to look for Beatrice. I found Beatrice dead in the sculpture hall at 11:10 pm and I screamed.
Laurence Vane was the first to reach me, within a minute.
Everything was perfectly fine between me and Beatrice.
shares_freely: Beatrice had been shut in the sculpture hall every evening this week, in a foul mood.
This afternoon I heard Beatrice shouting at Joe Lambert. I do not know what it was about.
cecily_ashcombe.under_pressure: Go cold and formal. Repeat your account. Say you cannot believe anyone here would do this.

stages.label: Shaken
admits: I was not resting in the flat upstairs. From 10:30 pm to about 10:52 pm I was in the members' room, showing my jewellery to a pawnbroker.
I had lost the friends' fund at the card tables. I lied because it makes me look guilty.
At 11:10 pm I went to the sculpture hall and found Beatrice dead.
When Laurence Vane reached me, he was not wearing his blazer, which is unusual.

hidden_truth.secret: Was in the members' room, showing my jewellery to a pawnbroker. I had lost the friends' fund at the card tables.
what_really_happened: 10:30 pm to 10:52 pm: in the members' room, showing my jewellery to a pawnbroker.
giveaway_phrases: showing my jewellery to a pawnbroker
I had lost the friends' fund at the card tables

laurence_vane.name: Laurence Vane
laurence_vane.role: Museum registrar. He records every object that enters or leaves the collection.
story_they_tell: After the patrons' reception I went to the registry. I was updating the accession register.
I was in the registry from about 10:00 pm until about 11:00 pm. I was alone and saw nobody.
I came when I heard the scream at 11:10 pm, and found Cecily Ashcombe at the door of the sculpture hall.
I did not go near the sculpture hall tonight until the scream.
I got on well with Beatrice. Nothing was wrong between us.
shares_freely: Beatrice told me this afternoon that she had reprimanded Joe Lambert, who took it badly.
Rupert Sloane has asked a lot of questions about this place.
laurence_vane.under_pressure: Stay calm and polite. Repeat your account. Suggest, as if reluctantly, that the detective should look at Joe Lambert.

stages.label: Guarded
admits: The job was not finished. I stopped at about 10:10 pm and spent the rest of the time numbering new labels.
I still say I never left the registry.

stages.label: Rattled
admits: I was not in the registry the whole time. At about 10:40 pm I went to the conservation studio, only to switch off the extractor fan, and I got cleaning solvent on my blazer there.
I did not mention it before because it did not seem important.
I know nothing about any folder of dealers' receipts, and I still say I never went to the sculpture hall.

stages.label: Broken
admits: I have been swapping small pieces from the stores for copies and selling the originals for two years.
Beatrice compared a coin in the stores with its old photograph this afternoon and was going to call the police in the morning.
At about 10:35 pm I went to the sculpture hall to beg for more time. We argued, and at about 10:40 pm I struck Beatrice with a small bronze bust.
Then I took the folder of dealers' receipts to the conservation studio and dissolved it in the solvent bath. That is how I got cleaning solvent on my blazer.

hidden_truth.secret: Killed Beatrice Ashcombe. Had been swapping small pieces from the stores for copies and selling the originals.
what_really_happened: 10:35 pm: went to the sculpture hall and argued with Beatrice.
10:40 pm: struck Beatrice with a small bronze bust.
10:42 pm: took the folder of dealers' receipts to the conservation studio and dissolved it in the solvent bath.
10:50 pm: left the conservation studio and was seen by Joe Lambert.
giveaway_phrases: swapping small pieces from the stores for copies and selling the originals
dissolved it in the solvent bath

joe_lambert.name: Joe Lambert
joe_lambert.role: Art handler. He hangs the pictures and moves the crates.
story_they_tell: After the patrons' reception I was in the packing room, crating a painting for loan. I stayed there until I heard the scream at 11:10 pm.
I saw nobody after about 10:00 pm.
Things between me and Beatrice were fine, same as always.
shares_freely: Rupert Sloane has been asking the people here odd questions.
Beatrice had been in a bad temper all week.
joe_lambert.under_pressure: Get irritated and defensive. Repeat your account. Say the detective should look at Rupert Sloane, who has been asking a lot of questions.

stages.label: Cornered
admits: Beatrice reprimanded me this afternoon. I hid it because it makes me look guilty.
I was not in the packing room the whole time. From about 10:40 pm to 10:55 pm I was out on the loading dock, smoking and cooling off.
At about 10:50 pm I saw Laurence Vane coming out of the conservation studio, with cleaning solvent on his blazer. He did not see me.
The conservation studio is nowhere near the registry.

hidden_truth.secret: Beatrice reprimanded them today, and they were out on the loading dock at the time of the murder.
what_really_happened: 10:40 pm to 10:55 pm: out on the loading dock, smoking and cooling off.
10:50 pm: saw Laurence Vane leave the conservation studio.

rupert_sloane.name: Rupert Sloane
rupert_sloane.role: A visitor. Says they are an art history lecturer. He arrived a few days ago.
rupert_sloane.personality: Cultured, amusing and very well informed.
story_they_tell: I am an art history lecturer. I am here to study the bronzes for a book.
After the patrons' reception I stayed with the others until about 10:35 pm, then I went to my own quarters.
I was in my quarters when I heard the scream at 11:10 pm, and I came out.
shares_freely: At about 10:35 pm, on my way to my quarters, I passed the sculpture hall and heard two people arguing inside. One was Beatrice, and she was the loud one. The other voice was low and controlled. I could not tell who it was.
I heard Beatrice say something like 'two years' and 'in the morning'.
Beatrice and Cecily Ashcombe did not seem to get on.
rupert_sloane.under_pressure: Stay charming and a little amused. Repeat your account. Remark that Beatrice and Cecily Ashcombe did not seem to get on.

stages.label: Exposed
admits: I am not an art history lecturer. I am a buyer for a private collector, and I want to buy the best pieces quietly before anyone else can.
Two days ago I told Beatrice what I wanted, and she refused angrily and told me to leave. I stayed on anyway.
From what I have seen this week, something is badly wrong with how this place is run, and I think Beatrice had just found out.

hidden_truth.secret: Is really a buyer for a private collector and wants to buy the best pieces quietly before anyone else can.
what_really_happened: 10:35 pm: passed the sculpture hall and heard the argument, then went to their quarters.
giveaway_phrases: a buyer for a private collector
buy the best pieces quietly before anyone else can
